input: read ./prompt.md and follow the instructions there

doc_friction.issue: The craft checklist says to check every number a character says against the note's model, but it doesn't mention the per-person counts a scene implies. My first draft had 41 cards naming one person, where the model gives about 3 (640 x 60 / 11,800). The fourth pass's 'count what a scene shows' rule covers this only loosely.

--for-changes on a story-only diff ran for more than 13 minutes, mostly portfolio-validate and the pages test job, and outlasted two wait_for calls. CI finished all 20 checks in about 4 minutes, so the local run added nothing and I stopped it.

notes: Project: Hearth & Horizon (creative_due drew it). Piece: the-ones-their-friends-name (4,934 words, text only: audio is at 577 MB against the 400 MB cap). Claimed with a Drafting commit and draft PR #18110 before writing. The model was simulated in a scratch script: 400 random configuration-model networks; coverage 14/29/21/38 in 100 for rule only, lottery, next-of-kin and named friend. The adversarial re-read caught (1) card tallies far above what the model implies, now Poisson-consistent, and (2) a timeline where the wave ran past the 23 November final scene, fixed by moving the second batch to 7 December. Every weekday was checked with Python. I also added a new H&H Next up proposal (optimal stopping), since the shelf's list was empty, and three subjects to subjects.txt (H&H had 0 unused). Verification: node --test in ventures/hearth-and-horizon 20/20; check_posts ok; PR CI 20 checks, all success or skipped. The local run_workflow_locally reported pages, ventures-tests (5/5) and portfolio-validate (100/100) passing before I stopped it in the pages test job.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: about 6 h for a writer to research, model and draft a 5,000-word hard-SF story with a worked network model

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
CI minutes and the reviewer bots' own model calls
